question.problem:
In the diagram below, $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$, while $\mathbf{i'}$ and $\mathbf{j'}$ are their images under the linear transformation $\mathbf T.$
What is the standard matrix of $\mathbf T?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/4d1b9e56c0c6214d949d12f45fe4aecea5516971203724ecf573a2b17c6e959a.png)
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that

- the image of $\mathbf{i}$ is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/95f30188b01782a32f4dbfdf48aae31e06846b0faa4a6f741e921ad64910221b.svg) and

- the image of $\mathbf{j}$ is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/0f695a9b9d87ca060eb5011b616d77b7e7d8d9394de6d537a2f2aab759c26a86.svg)

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156544/assets/a28158d8b163a3ec2ef4c568f7a4bbc63cf8b89385117a1e6178193d7cba886a.svg)
